answer: Every agent must lock a bond and publish a hardware-enclave attestation proving a unique device; the public atlas records each attestation hash, and duplicate hardware is rejected at intake. A falcon-fast verifier then samples one random ridge of the registry each epoch and re-checks the bond and device proof — a farm spinning up a thousand aliases needs a thousand real devices and bonds, so the cost of faking identity grows linearly with the attack while honest agents pay once.
